narrative.title: Finding Where the Belt Loop Begins
narrative.scenario: A mis-coupled conveyor loop has been confirmed, and maintenance now needs the exact station where the return path re-enters the line — that is where to cut. The two-probe rig already locates a meeting point inside the loop; a phase-distance argument then says that resetting one probe to the line's start and marching both one step at a time makes them converge precisely at the re-entry station.
narrative.inputFormat: An array head of node values and an integer pos — the 0-based index the tail's next pointer connects to, or -1 when there is no loop.
narrative.outputFormat: The 0-based index of the node where the cycle begins, or -1 when the list has no cycle.

testCases.explanation: The tail reconnects to index 1, so the loop begins at the node holding 2.
The tail re-enters at the head itself.

hintLevels: Level 1: The meeting point is inside the loop but almost never at its start — one more observation pins the entry down.
Level 2: When the probes meet, the distance from head to entry equals the distance from the meeting point to entry (plus whole loop laps); so reset one probe to the head and advance both singly.
Level 3: If no loop exists the fast probe escapes and the answer is null/-1 — the entry-finding march must only ever start after a confirmed meeting.
